newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends firmer ahead of election results.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends firmer ahead of election results.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended firmer at C$1.3735 (US$0.7280) from Friday's close of C$1.3770 (US$0.7262) on Monday in light trading ahead of results from the Canadian election today.
* Traders said the currency strengthened on late afternoon position-squaring after orders to buy Canadian dollars appeared in the market.
"I think you get any majority government and you'll see Canada strengthen," the trader said.

Canada's ruling Liberals have led the other main parties in the polls, despite indications that Prime Minister Jean Chretien may form his next government with a reduced majority and possibly a minority.

Currency analysts and dealers also said Canada's dollar might have benefited from a buy North American flurry after a Socialist party election victory in France and the ongoing battle between the German government and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of the bank's gold reserves.
The U.S. dollar rose to near one-month highs against the mark, as German and French political turmoil raised questions about the strength of Europe's planned single currency.

Concerns that France's new Socialist government would pursue a looser monetary policy than its center-right predecessor initially drove the mark higher, but comments from German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick spooked investors out of Europe and into U.S. dollars.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 84.85 yen from Friday's close of 84.33 yen and jumped to 1.2579 marks from Friday's 1.2380 marks.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
